key_insight: The paper argues that AI in healthcare should be judged by “alignment plausibility”: clear values, training that embeds them, and ongoing oversight that together support safe, beneficial behavior.
clinical_relevance: For mental health and other clinical uses of LLMs, this frames safety as more than avoiding obvious errors—it also means reducing dependency, boundary erosion, and harmful reinforcement over time.
method: Define explicit clinical values and norms as the target for alignment
Train models to reflect those values during development
Use deployment oversight to detect drift and longer-term harms, similar to clinical supervision
evidence_signal: This is a conceptual/regulatory proposal based on a literature-informed argument in the abstract, not on new clinical trial data or model benchmarking results.
watch_item: A major implementation challenge is turning broad clinical values into measurable standards and proving that oversight can reliably detect subtle harms after deployment.
paper_title: Alignment Plausibility: A New Standard for Assuring AI in Healthcare
